title: Peeling Cabinet Paint: Quick Fix and Permanent Fix
description: Why cabinet paint peels, how to stabilize a chipping door with a quick touch-up today, and what a permanent refinish takes so it stops for good.
h1: A Temporary Fix for Peeling Cabinet Paint (and the Permanent One)
heroIntro: A chipping cabinet door can be patched in an afternoon, and that buys time. But if the paint is peeling in sheets, the cause is underneath it, and only a proper refinish makes it stop.
excerpt: Why cabinet paint peels, how to patch a chipping door today, and what a permanent refinish takes so it stops for good.

body: When paint lifts off cabinets in strips or flakes, it is almost always an adhesion problem, not a paint-quality problem. The common causes are:
bullets: Grease left on the surface. Kitchen cabinets collect a thin film of cooking oil that you cannot see. Paint over it never bonds properly.
No bonding primer. Factory cabinet finishes are hard, slick lacquers or catalyzed coatings, and most paints will not grip them without sanding and a primer designed to bond.
Wall paint used on cabinets. Standard wall paint stays relatively soft and can be scraped or peeled from cabinet surfaces.
Moisture and heat: steam from the dishwasher, kettle, or range, and water splashing around the sink.
Rehanging doors too soon, before the paint has hardened, so it sticks to frames and tears off.

sections.h2: Diagnose: spot problem or system failure?
body: Look at where the paint is failing. Chips on the edges of a few doors near the handles, or a dent where a pot hit, are wear-and-tear spots that can be touched up. Paint that peels in sheets, that you can lift with a fingernail or tape, or that is failing on most doors indicates the entire coating has poor adhesion.

Try a quick tape test on an intact area: press painter's tape firmly onto the paint, then pull it off quickly. If paint comes off with the tape, the whole system is failing, and touch-ups will be a temporary measure only.

Also note where the peeling starts. Failure that begins on the lower edges of sink-base doors or around the dishwasher points to water. Failure on uppers next to the range points to grease and heat. Paint that peels cleanly off in one piece, showing a shiny surface underneath, means it never bonded to the factory finish at all. Each clue tells you what has to change in the next paint job so the problem does not repeat.
If your home was built before 1978 and the cabinets have older paint layers, test for lead before sanding or scraping, and follow lead-safe practices if the result is positive.

sections.h2: The temporary fix: stabilizing a chipped door
body: If you need the kitchen to look presentable now, for a holiday, an inspection, or a home sale, this fix will hold for a while on small areas:
bullets: Clean the area with a degreaser, not an oil soap, then rinse and dry.
Remove all loose paint around the chip with a putty knife; anything lifting will keep lifting.
Sand the edges with 220-grit paper until they feather smoothly into the surrounding paint.
Wipe away dust, then dab on a bonding primer only where wood or the old finish is exposed.
Fill deep chips with a small amount of wood filler or spackle, sand smooth, and spot-prime again.
Touch up with the original cabinet paint using a small artist's brush or foam brush, applying thin coats.
Let it cure for several days before heavy use, and leave the door slightly open while it hardens.

sections.h2: The permanent fix: refinish the right way
body: When adhesion has failed across the cabinets, the only lasting fix is to remove the failing coating and rebuild the finish properly. The process includes:
bullets: Removing doors, drawers, and hardware, and labelling everything.
Stripping or sanding off all loose and poorly bonded paint. Where paint is mostly sound, a thorough scuff-sand may be enough.
Thoroughly degreasing every surface, including the backs of doors and the face frames.
Applying a bonding primer suited to the substrate, with a stain-blocking primer on oak or other tannin-rich woods.
Spraying two coats of waterborne urethane enamel or another cabinet-grade enamel, with light sanding between coats.
Curing the doors flat before rehanging and adding soft-close bumpers.

body: A few common shortcuts make peeling worse. Do not spread a fresh coat of wall paint over the whole door to hide the chips; it will bond only to the loose layer below and lift with it. Avoid caulk or glue under flaking edges, which leaves lumps that show through any future finish. And do not reach for heavy-duty chemical strippers indoors without strong ventilation and the right gloves and eye protection. When in doubt, take the doors to a garage or covered porch to work on them.

sections.h2: Caring for painted cabinets in a Florida kitchen
body: Humidity in North Central Florida homes slows the curing of fresh paint and keeps kitchens damper than you might expect. A few habits keep a good finish looking good:
bullets: Wipe cabinets with a mild degreaser or dish soap solution, not an oil soap, which leaves a residue that can interfere with future touch-ups.
Run the range hood when cooking and vent steam away from cabinet faces; open the dishwasher only after it has cooled.
Dry water splashes around the sink quickly, especially on the lower edges of doors.
Keep the labelled touch-up paint and fix small chips before moisture gets under the edges.

body: A few chips can be handled by most homeowners. Widespread peeling is different: stripping and refinishing a full kitchen takes considerable time, dust control, and spray equipment for a smooth result. If the cabinets are oak, read our guide on painting oak cabinets, which covers grain filling and tannin blocking. faqs.q: Why is my newly painted cabinet paint peeling?
faqs.a: The most common reasons are grease left on the surface, no bonding primer over a slick factory finish, wall paint instead of cabinet enamel, or doors rehung before the paint cured.

faqs.q: Can I just paint over peeling cabinet paint?
faqs.a: No. New paint will only be as well bonded as the layer under it. Remove all loose paint, sand, degrease, and prime before recoating, or the peeling will continue.

faqs.q: What is the best way to clean painted cabinets?
faqs.a: Use a mild degreaser or a dish soap and water solution with a soft cloth, then wipe dry. Avoid abrasive pads and oil soaps.

faqs.q: How long does a cabinet touch-up last?
faqs.a: A properly prepared touch-up on a small chip can last a long time if the surrounding paint is well bonded. If the coating is failing overall, touch-ups are only a short-term measure.
